---
title: "What assumptions have we made so far, can you rank them by severity?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

Each assumption is swapped for the other readings the plan allows, one at a
time with everything else held fixed at 6 m/s, and severity is read as the
spread it opens in the nose ballast needed for 10% MAC — the conclusion this
chapter has actually drawn.

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed
Two assumptions cannot be swung inside this model at all — the section standing
in for a sharp-edged plate, and the airframe being rigid and true. They are
named in the answer rather than plotted.
:::

```{python}
def assess(airplane, mp, band=(0, 8), V=6.0):
    """
    Neutral point, best L/D, and the nose ballast for 10% MAC.

    No moment reference is passed: `neutral_point` reads it off the airplane,
    so a variant that moves a surface cannot be measured from the wrong
    station.
    """
    x_np = neutral_point(airplane, band=band, V=V)
    p = polars(ALPHA_SWEEP, V=V, airplane=airplane)
    x_cg = x_np - 0.10 * c_w
    return x_np, (np.array(p["CL"]) / np.array(p["CD"])).max(), \
        ballast_for(x_cg, 0.0, mp)


def wing_at(x_le, curved_is_le=False, tip_rise=None):
    """The wing rebuilt at a chosen root LE station, optionally flipped."""
    rise = z_tip if tip_rise is None else tip_rise
    return asb.Wing(name="Wing", symmetric=True, xsecs=[
        asb.WingXSec(
            xyz_le=[x_le + ((wing_c[0] - c) if curved_is_le else 0),
                    eta * b_w / 2, eta * rise],
            chord=c, airfoil=airfoil,
        )
        for eta, c in zip(wing_eta, wing_c)
    ])


def with_wing(wing, x_ref):
    base = build_airplane()
    return asb.Airplane(
        name="variant", wings=[wing] + list(base.wings[1:]),
        fuselages=base.fuselages, s_ref=S_w, c_ref=c_w, b_ref=b_w,
        xyz_ref=[x_ref, 0, 0],
    )


def mass_with_wing_at(x_le):
    """The wing carries mass as well as lift, so moving it moves the CG."""
    global x_le_w
    saved, x_le_w = x_le_w, x_le
    try:
        return mass_properties()
    finally:
        x_le_w = saved
```

```{python}
mp0 = mass_properties()
base = assess(mceagle, mp0)

cases = {}

# The "Mount wings here" bracket runs 119.2 to 166.4 mm aft of the nose -- 47 mm
# against a 99 mm root chord, so it cannot be marking the chord. The model
# centres the chord on it; the alternatives pin one end of the chord instead.
wing_stations = [0.1664 - wing_c[0], 0.1192]   # chord pinned aft, then forward
cases["wing station on its mount bracket"] = [
    assess(with_wing(wing_at(xl), xl + 0.25 * wing_c[0]), mass_with_wing_at(xl))
    for xl in wing_stations
]

# "A slight negative angle to the plane of the wings", with no number given.
cases["stabilizer incidence, 0 to -4 deg"] = [
    assess(build_airplane(stab_incidence=inc), mp0) for inc in [0.0, -4.0]
]

# 5 mm foam on the mean chord is 5.7% thick; the section stands in for a flat
# plate, and the sheet thickness that picks it is itself assumed.
_af = airfoil
cases["section standing in for flat foam"] = []
for _name in ["naca0004", "naca0008"]:
    airfoil = asb.Airfoil(_name)
    cases["section standing in for flat foam"].append(assess(build_airplane(), mp0))
airfoil = _af

# The wing is traced with one straight edge and one curved; which is the
# leading edge is a reading of the plan, not a measurement. Flipping it also
# moves the wing's own centroid, hence the mass offset.
cases["which wing edge is the leading edge"] = [
    base,
    assess(with_wing(wing_at(x_le_w, curved_is_le=True), x_qc_w),
           mass_with_wing_at(x_le_w + wing_c[0] - 2 * 0.0450)),
]

# The neutral point comes from a straight-line fit whose band is a choice.
cases["neutral-point fit band"] = [
    assess(mceagle, mp0, band=b) for b in [(0, 6), (2, 10)]
]

# Glue is not in the mass build-up at all. It lies where the fuselage lies.
cases["glue, currently not modelled"] = [
    (base[0], base[1],
     ballast_for(base[0] - 0.10 * c_w, 0.0,
                 mp0 + asb.MassProperties(mass=m, x_cg=0.1163)))
    for m in [0.0, 3.0e-3]
]

cases["operating speed, 4 to 8 m/s"] = [
    assess(mceagle, mp0, V=V) for V in [4.0, 8.0]
]

# The plan's 2.5 cm tip rise, scaled as an angle or kept as a length.
cases["dihedral, 9.6 or 13.3 deg"] = [
    base, assess(with_wing(wing_at(x_le_w, tip_rise=0.025), x_qc_w), mp0)
]

_shape = fus_shape
cases["fuselage cross-section exponent"] = []
for fus_shape in [2.0, 10.0]:
    cases["fuselage cross-section exponent"].append(assess(build_airplane(), mp0))
fus_shape = _shape

order = sorted(cases, key=lambda k: -abs(cases[k][1][2] - cases[k][0][2]))
span = lambda k, i: (min(cases[k][0][i], cases[k][1][i]),
                     max(cases[k][0][i], cases[k][1][i]))

b_wing = span("wing station on its mount bracket", 2)
n_wing = span("wing station on its mount bracket", 0)
b_stab = span("stabilizer incidence, 0 to -4 deg", 2)
b_band = span("neutral-point fit band", 2)
b_sect = span("section standing in for flat foam", 2)
b_edge = span("which wing edge is the leading edge", 2)
b_glue = span("glue, currently not modelled", 2)
# How far the neutral point moves per mm the wing moves.
np_per_wing = (n_wing[1] - n_wing[0]) / (wing_stations[1] - wing_stations[0])
ld_V = span("operating speed, 4 to 8 m/s", 1)
# Speed is excluded here: it is the one arm L/D is NOT indifferent to, and
# folding it in would make the sentence quote its own counterexample.
_geom = [k for k in cases if k != "operating speed, 4 to 8 m/s"]
ld_all = (min(span(k, 1)[0] for k in _geom), max(span(k, 1)[1] for k in _geom))
```

**Answer.** No single assumption dominates. Five sit within a factor of about
`{python} f"{(b_wing[1]-b_wing[0])/(b_edge[1]-b_edge[0]):.1f}"` of one another
and together set the answer; below them the rest are noise (@tbl-severity).

Largest is where the wing sits along the fuselage: the plan's mount bracket is
47 mm long against a 99 mm root chord, so it cannot be marking the chord, and
the readings it permits move the neutral point between
`{python} f"{n_wing[0]*1e3:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{n_wing[1]*1e3:.1f}"` mm — the
neutral point tracks the wing at about `{python} f"{np_per_wing:.2f}"` mm per
mm — and the ballast between
`{python} f"{b_wing[1]*1e3:.2f}"` and `{python} f"{b_wing[0]*1e3:.2f}"` g. Then,
in order: the stabilizer incidence, which the plan describes only as "a slight
negative angle" (`{python} f"{b_stab[0]*1e3:.2f}"`–`{python} f"{b_stab[1]*1e3:.2f}"` g);
the fit band chosen for the neutral point
(`{python} f"{b_band[0]*1e3:.2f}"`–`{python} f"{b_band[1]*1e3:.2f}"` g); the
section standing in for flat foam, together with the 5 mm thickness that picks
it (`{python} f"{b_sect[0]*1e3:.2f}"`–`{python} f"{b_sect[1]*1e3:.2f}"` g); and
which of the wing's two edges is the leading one
(`{python} f"{b_edge[0]*1e3:.2f}"`–`{python} f"{b_edge[1]*1e3:.2f}"` g). That the
fit band — a choice made in the analysis, not in the aircraft — ranks third is
worth noting. Glue, absent from the mass build-up entirely, only ever helps: it
lies forward of the structure CG, so 3 g of it cuts the ballast to
`{python} f"{b_glue[0]*1e3:.2f}"` g.

Ballast is not the whole story. Best L/D is nearly indifferent to every
geometric arm above — it moves only `{python} f"{ld_all[0]:.2f}"` to
`{python} f"{ld_all[1]:.2f}"` across all of them — and is set instead by the
speed the polar is read at,
`{python} f"{ld_V[0]:.2f}"` at 4 m/s against `{python} f"{ld_V[1]:.2f}"` at
8 m/s. Dihedral and the fuselage cross-section exponent are negligible for
anything computed here, though dihedral is a roll-axis device being judged on a
pitch-axis result and no lateral case has been run.

Two assumptions cannot be swung inside this model. The first is `AeroBuildup`
with NeuralFoil section data standing in for a square-cut foam plate at
Re 3.6 × 10⁴: the sweep above only substitutes smooth NACA sections, while the
real leading edge separates at once, so the best L/D here is optimistic by an
amount this chapter cannot bound. The second is that the airframe is rigid and
true, when the plan's own trimming instructions are to warp the fin.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-severity
#| tbl-cap: "Each assumption swung across the readings the plan allows, ordered by the spread it opens in the ballast. Both arms are shown for every quantity."
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame({
    "assumption": order,
    "neutral point [mm]": [f"{span(k,0)[0]*1e3:.1f} – {span(k,0)[1]*1e3:.1f}" for k in order],
    "best L/D": [f"{span(k,1)[0]:.2f} – {span(k,1)[1]:.2f}" for k in order],
    "ballast [g]": [f"{span(k,2)[0]*1e3:.2f} – {span(k,2)[1]*1e3:.2f}" for k in order],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-severity
#| fig-cap: "Nose ballast required for 10% MAC, as each assumption is swung across the readings the plan allows. Bars span the two arms; the dot marks where the current model sits. Ordered by span."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.2))

lo = np.array([span(k, 2)[0] for k in order]) * 1e3
hi = np.array([span(k, 2)[1] for k in order]) * 1e3
y = np.arange(len(order))[::-1]

ax.barh(y, hi - lo, left=lo, height=0.45, color="#4C78A8", zorder=2,
        label="span of the two arms")
ax.plot(np.full(len(order), base[2] * 1e3), y, "o", ms=6, color="0.15",
        zorder=3, label="current model")

ax.set_yticks(y, order)
ax.set_xlabel("nose ballast for 10% MAC [g]")
ax.set_xlim(0, 5)
ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.3)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
for side in ["top", "right", "left"]:
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(loc="lower left", frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
